title: High Speed Rail Planning Authority Bill 2016
short_title: High Speed Rail Planning Authority Bill 2016

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would establish a High Speed Rail Planning Authority to advise on, plan and develop an east coast rail network and preserve its corridor.
The authority would have eleven members, combining ministerial appointees with nominees from relevant state and territory governments, local government and the railway industry.
Its work would include land use planning and public consultation, and the Act would commence when a budget appropriation is made for the authority’s operation.
changes: A statutory authority would be created with powers necessary to carry out its functions.
Members would be appointed for three-year terms.
The authority could engage staff and consultants.
The minister could make supporting rules by legislative instrument.
summary.affected: The authority, nominating governments, the Australian Local Government Association, the Australasian Railway Association and people consulted on rail planning are affected.
